text:
Operations Analyst – Fenwick Freight Solutions

Fenwick Freight Solutions, a family-owned haulier with depots in six countries, is expanding its analytics team. We are looking for an Operations Analyst who will [1] raw shipment data into clear recommendations for depot managers.

[2] You will work alongside experienced planners, and you will be encouraged to challenge established practice where the evidence supports a different approach. The post suits a candidate with a quantitative degree and at least two years' experience of logistics or a related field. [3] prior knowledge of our routing software is not required, applicants must be [4] with advanced spreadsheet functions and at least one query language.

questions.explanation: Analysts 'translate' data into recommendations, meaning convert it; 'transcend' means go beyond, 'transmit' means send, and 'transplant' means move.

choices: The role offers an unusually indirect route from analysis to action, since managers act on most recommendations within a year.
The role offers an unusually direct route from analysis to action, since managers act on most recommendations within a week.
The role offers an unusually direct route from analysis to action, although managers rarely act on recommendations.
The role offered an unusually direct route from analysis to action, since managers acted on most recommendations within a week.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says the analyst will work with planners and challenge practice, which presupposes real influence; only the first option gives that. The others describe an indirect route, say managers ignore recommendations, or use a past tense.
'While prior knowledge ... is not required' concedes a limit before the stronger demand; 'because' and 'whenever' do not fit, and 'provided' needs 'that'.
A candidate must be 'proficient with' functions, meaning skilled; 'prolific' means productive, 'profound' means deep, and 'prominent' means well known.

text:
Aldwych Concert Hall – Ticket Exchange and Refund Policy

Tickets may be exchanged for another performance of the same program up to forty-eight hours before the start, [1] a fee of £5 per ticket. Exchanges are subject to availability, and no refund will be made where the replacement performance carries a lower price.

[2] Where a performance is canceled by the hall, ticket holders will be offered a full refund or a credit valid for twelve months. The hall cannot, [3], accept responsibility for travel or accommodation costs incurred by patrons. Patrons who are unable to attend because of illness may request a credit, [4] they supply a medical certificate within seven days of the performance.

questions.explanation: 'Subject to a fee' means on payment of one; 'subjected to' implies suffering, and the other forms are ungrammatical.

choices: The hall reserves the right to substitute artists or alter programs, in which case an exchange or refund will be offered.
The hall reserves the right to substitute artists or alter programs, in which case no exchange or refund will be offered.
The hall reserves the right to change the date or venue, in which case no exchange or refund will be offered.
The hall reserved the right to substitute artists, in which case no exchange or refund was offered.
questions.explanation: The next sentence contrasts with the previous one: 'Where a performance is canceled' gives a different outcome (refund). So the previous sentence must state a case where no refund applies; only the first does. The others offer a refund, change the date, or use a past tense.
'The hall cannot, however, accept responsibility' contrasts with the refund promise; 'therefore', 'moreover' and 'similarly' do not.
'Provided that they supply a medical certificate' sets the condition for the credit; the others misstate the logic or are not conjunctions of condition.

text:
Subject: Revised timetable for the audit

Dear Mr. Hallström,

Further to your request, I have revised the timetable for the interim audit of your Gothenburg subsidiary. Fieldwork will now begin on 9 October, [1] a week later than originally planned, to accommodate the system migration that your team has scheduled for the preceding weekend.

[2] The delay will not affect the date of the final report, as we propose to run the testing of controls and the review of inventory counts in parallel. [3] you could confirm by Wednesday that the migration is on schedule, we shall be able to book the necessary staff. Should the date change again, we would [4] the right to adjust our fee accordingly.

questions.explanation: 'That is, a week later than originally planned' restates the date in other words; 'namely' introduces a list and 'moreover' and 'otherwise' do not clarify.

choices: I appreciate that this arrangement is ideal, but it should maximize disruption to your own finance staff.
I appreciate that this arrangement is not ideal, but it should minimize disruption to your own finance staff.
I appreciate that this arrangement is not ideal, and it should minimize disruption to our own audit staff.
I appreciated that this arrangement was not ideal, but it minimized disruption to your own finance staff.
questions.explanation: The next sentence reassures the client that the final report date is unaffected, continuing a conciliatory tone. Only the first sentence is consistent: it concedes the drawback and promises minimal disruption. The others are illogical, change the subject to audit staff, or use a past tense.
'I should be grateful if you could confirm' is the standard polite request; the others are ungrammatical or inappropriate.
The firm will 'reserve the right' to adjust its fee; after 'would' the base verb is required.
